audience.summary: UK commercial building maintenance and building services firms

cta.organic: Organic posts give practical value without hard selling. Don't push the CTA in every post.

brand.imagery: Realistic UK commercial maintenance imagery: plant rooms, rooftops, risers, service vans and engineers at work. No stock-photo clichés.
brand.logoRule: Use the official Nexai logo (set in Prism’s Photo layout).

writing.voice: Write like we’re giving someone an honest update from inside Nexai. Use natural British English and first-person plural where it fits. Explain what we’re building, what prompted it, the everyday problem and the outcome we’re working towards. Give the reader something useful. Distinguish work in progress from products, results or client work we can genuinely point to. When a CTA fits, invite a comment or message in our own voice. Vary the wording. Some posts can end on the useful point.

items.name: Professional Websites
items.audience: UK commercial building maintenance and building services firms, particularly owners, MDs and operations directors
items.publicWording: Fast, clear websites for commercial maintenance and building services firms that explain what you do and make it easy for facilities and property managers to get in touch.
items.problem: Facilities and property managers judge a maintenance firm by its website, and many sites don’t explain what the firm does or make it easy to get in touch.
items.outcome: A clear website that explains what you do and makes it easy for the right clients to get in touch.
headline: Clear websites
for maintenance firms.
items.visual: A maintenance firm’s website open on a laptop in a site office, engineer’s van visible through the window.

items.name: Custom Business Software

items.publicWording: Software built around how your engineers and office actually work: job management, job sheets, photos, sign-off and invoicing in one place.

items.name: Nexai Revenue Recovery
items.audience: Local SMEs that already hold customer data
items.problem: Revenue left behind in past customers, open quotes and missed enquiries.
items.outcome: Recover revenue from contacts a business already has.
items.internalNotes: Product family name. Keep internal until approved for public use.

items.name: Database Reactivation
items.audience: Local SMEs across sectors with an existing customer database
items.problem: Customers who were happy with the work often never hear from the business again, so repeat work and referrals go to whoever got in touch last.
items.outcome: A simple, respectful way to reconnect with past customers and turn some of those relationships into repeat work.
items.publicWording: We’re building a way for businesses to reconnect with past customers they already have on their books, so good relationships don’t quietly go cold.
items.internalNotes: First build, in development. Proposed commercial model (not approved for public use): no upfront development fee; the client covers running costs plus a commission on sales it generates. Client contact lists stay in the client’s own systems, never in Marketing HQ.
headline: Past customers,
back in touch.
items.visual: Owner of a small UK business at their desk, looking back through past jobs and customer notes on a laptop; warm, natural light.

items.name: Quote Recovery
items.problem: Quotes go out and are never followed up, so work the business could have won goes quiet.
items.outcome: Follow up outstanding quotes so fewer go cold.

items.name: Enquiry Capture
items.problem: New enquiries slip through when the team is busy on site.
items.outcome: Capture and follow up every new enquiry promptly.
